reasons.reason: Self-serve plans bill monthly only, with no annual-prepay discount to lower the rate.

picks.why: Creator and Creator Pro both give two free months on annual billing from their very first paid tier, starting at $39 a month, with no contact-count minimum to unlock it.
Its annual pre-pay saves about 15%, available on every tier of its $350 Premium plan from the start, and on Essentials and Standard once a list passes 10,000 contacts.

reasons.reason: You pay the same price whether or not your list is actually tied to a Shopify or WooCommerce order history.

picks.why: Every plan, including Free, already includes purchase-behavior tracking and personalized product recommendations, so a business without a store catalog isn't paying extra for Klaviyo's order-volume-priced Reviews add-on to get similar insight.
Built around a creator's newsletter rather than a store's order data, with a free plan covering up to 10,000 subscribers and no product catalog assumed anywhere in the product.

reasons.reason: Composer, Customer Hub, Social Marketing and Reviews are separate paid add-ons stacked on the Email plan, not one bundled price.

picks.why: Marketing automation and a CRM are built into every paid plan, Starter included, from $15 a month billed annually at 1,000 contacts, rather than sold as separate products layered on top.

Its $97 Starter plan already bundles a CRM, a funnel and site builder, and prices email and SMS as metered usage instead of a stacked subscription; its AI agent is the one extra sold as a recurring add-on, at $50 or $97 per location.

reasons.reason: Cross your active-profile tier and Klaviyo moves you to a pricier plan automatically, and MMS, WhatsApp and RCS rates aren't published anywhere you can check first.

picks.why: Its $97 Starter plan doesn't move with your contact count at all, and its help center publishes exact per-message rates for MMS and WhatsApp, filling the gap where Klaviyo's own calculator showed no usable rate for those same channels.

reasons.reason: There's no trial of the paid Email plan or its add-ons, only a capped free-forever tier.

picks.why: Its 14-day trial needs no credit card and runs on Professional-plan features, so you can use the fuller paid product before committing to it, not just a capped free tier.

reasons.reason: Cancel mid-cycle instead of waiting for renewal and Klaviyo keeps the rest of that month's payment.

picks.why: Every paid plan, including annual ones, carries a 30-day money-back guarantee, so cancelling partway through a cycle isn't automatically a forfeited month the way it is on Klaviyo.
